So glad I found this hotel. It's not as central as the Rex but, quite honestly, with this buffet restaurant there is no need to go anywhere. Dinner and breakfast at the Canvas are just divine. Excellent service from Max, Tyler and their teams of servers and chefs. Super attentive and allergy-conscious. Foie gras is cooked to perfection, steaks, glorious dishes, fresh oysters (although I found the excessive rinsing of the shucked oyster somewhat disturbing, plus the adductor muscle is not cut), and the best passion fruit I have ever tasted. Breakfast is equally amazing with the singular availability of natto, plus the usual fresh fruits, lovely warm dishes and roasts. The "almost perfect" part of it comes with the eggs. Such a disappointment. Those eggs are old. Just not fresh at all. They break onto the pan and spread like a watery pancake. Old eggs are a turn off and a food safety risk. I saw the cartons and, although the supplier is reliable, the expiry date was within three days. That means these eggs had been on the counter for already almost three weeks - out of the fridge! The idea that hotels have to leave eggs on the counter is visually pretty, but not good for the eggs. Keep them in the fridge and break them onto a hot pan (not just warm), and you will have great dishes. Finally, the whole team needs to brush up their English, as this is an international hotel that is serving a diversity of nationalities. In spite of all this nitty gritty criticism, I love the place and it deserves full 5 marks on this site.
